chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Muhammad ibn Amer quoted his uncle Abdullah ibn Amer, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Ebad ibn Saheeb that he had heard Aba Abdullah (peace be upon him) say:
God will never grant a hypocrite or a corrupt person insight, knowledge and a good-temper.
ai.seo_question: What three qualities does God not grant to a hypocrite or corrupt person?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to establish a diagnostic criterion for spiritual authenticity, arguing that the simultaneous presence of deep jurisprudential insight (*fiqh*), noble conduct (*husn al-khuluq*), and dignified demeanor (*husn al-samt*) is rare in those who are fundamentally hypocritical or corrupt. This triad serves as a safeguard against superficial religiosity, ensuring that outward piety is matched by inner integrity and scholarly depth. The narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the unity of knowledge, action, and character as markers of true faith.
